guys.title: Brooklyn's backcourt
guys.take: Two of the most fun, most overlooked players in the league, and they share a small-market backcourt. Demin was a unicorn at BYU: a 6'9" guard with a lead guard's passing, almost 8 assists per 40. What sold me came at the end of last season, when the jumper got hot and you could see his game translating to the NBA. Traoré barely got talked about as a rookie. This year he's hard not to watch. He's that fast, and getting downhill against the best defenders in the world looks easy for him. I first caught word of him the year before the draft, when he was a teenager going at grown pros in France's top league. Now he's at 13.6 a night on 61% true shooting, producing like a top-7 pick in his class after going 19th.

guys.title: Bennett Stirtz
guys.take: I've been on Stirtz since Drake. I watched him run Ben McCollum's offense there, followed him to Iowa when McCollum moved, and saw him put up 19.8 a game against Big Ten defenses without forcing anything. The model agrees with me: he's a Connector, the archetype that has beaten its draft slot. Now he's in OKC, the best place in the league for a guy like this to develop, and he's already earning 18 minutes a night as a rookie on a deep roster. He's producing ahead of where he went at 16, and the minutes are only going up from here.

guys.title: Cedric Coward
guys.take: I followed Coward closely all of last year. A shoulder injury ended his only season at Washington State after six games, and that question mark followed him into the draft. He came back healthy and has been proving the doubters wrong ever since. Now he's starting every game for Memphis: 14.1 points and 8.8 rebounds a night on 60% true shooting, producing like the third-best player in his class. He's on pace for a big sophomore year.
